ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The shaded part in the figure is a trapezoid, with an inward-concave semicircular notch on the left side. The upper base of the trapezoid is labeled 6, and the lower base is labeled 14. The vertical dashed segment on the left is the diameter of the semicircle, and the length from near the midpoint of the dashed line to an endpoint is labeled 4, so the radius of the semicircle is 4, the diameter is 8, which is also the height of the trapezoid. Reasoning: First calculate the area of the complete trapezoid. Trapezoid area = ((upper base + lower base) / 2) × height = ((6 + 14) / 2) × 8 = 10 × 8 = 80. Semicircular notch area = (1/2) × π × 4^2 = 8π ≈ 25.1. Shaded area = 80 - 25.1 = 54.9.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a shaded trapezoid with a semicircular cutout on its left side. From the image, the parallel bases of the trapezoid are 6 and 14, and the semicircle has radius 4, so the trapezoid height is the semicircle diameter, 8. Compute the area of the full trapezoid: ((6+14)/2)*8 = 80. Then subtract the area of the semicircular cutout: (1/2)*pi*4^2 ≈ 25.1. The shaded area is 80 - 25.1 = 54.9.
